title: Adaptive flush + SLO-aware scheduler to cut first-byte streaming latency
author: Asha Kapoor
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-11-12 by Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: streaming-first-byte (FBT) tail has been a recurring customer pain point for low-latency applications. This change introduces an adaptive flush manager and an SLO-aware scheduler that cooperate with kernel pacing and the KV cache coalescer to prioritize first-token delivery while preserving aggregate throughput. Key ideas: 1) adaptive flush window: dynamically shorten/lengthen the stream flush cadence per-connection based on observed token emission rate and request SLO tag; 2) SLO-aware scheduler: lightweight scheduling tier that gives head-of-line progress to SLO-sensitive streams (configured via request metadata); 3) KV coalescer: batch small KV cache prefetches into a micro-prefetch window to avoid small-cache read stalls during the token loop; 4) non-blocking token loop: refactor to a lock-free fast path for single-token emitters and defer heavier work to background continuations. This PR includes microbenchmarks, canary configuration, and docs for tuning. Checklist: - [x] design doc: internal design link https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1428/adaptive-flush-design - [x] unit + integration tests for flush manager and scheduler - [x] performance microbenchmarks and perf-canary entry - [x] docs/streaming_tuning.md for ops knobs - [x] feature-flag guarded rollout and canary config Notes: this is behind feature flag streaming.adaptive_flush and slo_priority scheduling is opt-in by default. See dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming-adaptive-flush for before/after.

bench_results: local microbench median FBT: baseline 21.4ms -> adaptive 17.0ms (-20.6%)

notes: Rollout plan: feature-flag gated gradual rollout to canary hosts for 48h, promote to 20% traffic for 72h, monitor streaming.fbt_ms and tail_error_rate; automatic rollback if p95 increases by >5%. Ops knobs added: streaming.adaptive_flush.window_ms, streaming.adaptive_flush.decay_factor, streaming.slo_priority.enabled, kv.coalescer.coalesce_window_ms, kv.coalescer.max_batch_size.
release_notes: Improved streaming first-byte latency via adaptive flush cadence and SLO-aware scheduling; opt-in by default behind streaming.adaptive_flush. Operators can tune coalesce and flush windows for different workload profiles.
